reason: A small bird leans in to peck the top of an upright cone; the contact tips the rigid cone about its base rim until it lies on its side, while the bird keeps its feet planted and recoils.

total_plan.scene: Fixed floor plane at z=-0.6. A compact bird stands left of a small cone near the origin. The upright cone has base center about (0.12,0,-0.58), radius about 0.14, and apex about (0.12,0,-0.20). Bird feet are on the floor around (-0.32,0,-0.6), with torso behind/left and head/neck aimed toward the cone apex. A slight depth offset keeps the cone base ellipse and bird body contours readable in 3D.
total_plan.parts: Bird: round spatial body with a few intersecting contour curves, small head, pointed beak, single-line neck and two planted legs/feet, folded wing curves, and a short tail. Cone: rigid circular base drawn as an ellipse, an apex, and two or three straight side generators connecting rim to apex; stable dimensions, no texture. Floor serves only as support.
total_plan.motion: t=0: bird upright with neutral head, cone upright. t=.25: bird leans forward and extends its neck toward the apex, feet fixed. t=.5: beak tip contacts the cone apex exactly; cone is still upright. t=.75: after contact the beak pushes the apex toward +x, so the cone rotates clockwise about its floor-contact base rim; the opposite base rim lifts, and the bird's head follows slightly while its body stays balanced. t=1: the cone has toppled fully to +x and lies on its side supported by the floor, apex near (0.64,0,-0.58) and base left/up; the bird recoils and stands clear with feet still planted.
total_plan.constraints: Contact occurs before the cone rotates. Bird feet stay in fixed floor contact; the head and neck articulate rather than sliding a frozen pose. The cone is rigid: base radius and height never change. It pivots on the base rim on the floor until its lateral side and base rim settle on the floor in the final state. Final bird and cone are floor-supported, non-overlapping, with no trails, arrows, text, or extra scenery.
